units.translation: I do not know how I should distrust you.
I know these things.
For Xerxes, as I know, had a thousand.
For I know well that you are pondering these things.
I know the family.
I alone of the gods know the keys of the house.
They will fight over you, I know well.
Or do you not know precisely that you are overly wise, and that punishment is inflicted on a vain tongue?
Show, if indeed you know.
You then know how to cross over.
Do you know how to indicate clearly?
But if you truly know her fate.
If you know, tell me this willingly.
You know what it is to do wrong.
But you do not know the future.
But he knows that they must end the battle.
For if he knows any further remedy for evils.
For those whom someone sent, he knows.
But if truly, who knows?
No one knows.
He does not know what sort of tongue will be fashioned.
Aegisthus, if he knows, even though he is abroad.
And falling, he does not know this, under foolish ruin.
He does not know whence the blows of life come.

And in your fortunes, know, I grieve with you, where 'know' is inserted in the middle of the sentence like 'I know well' in the places indicated above, and likewise 'know well' or 'for you know well' in the places to be indicated below.
Know this well – do not tell me twice.
For know this well, never in one day did such a number of people die.
Know this well now, the evil is not yet at its height.
Know well that for the sake of the multitude the barbarians prevailed with their ships.
Know that you hear the truth.
Know that my judgment will not be corrupted.
But know that you are wretched from a bold heart.
Cast out by the people, know well, curses that bring stoning.
Know that you will give me recompense.
He will lift, know well, and cast before your eyes.
Know that a dear man's foal, bereft, is yoked.
For know, these things remain for your children and house, whichever you establish.
From these, then, know, a fine device.
Let him know, whoever is not winged, taught by anxieties.
For you know well, my son – he would become a wondrous man.
Having been taught, I would know this better.
So that you may know this.
So that she may know that she does not hear me in vain.
Let us know whether (thus Turnebus for 'or') we are victorious or defeated.

But so that you may know, for I do not know where it will end, – I turn the course further out. For thus it has been corrected from what is read in M: 'another would know this then – of the charioteer'.
Having sworn beforehand that I know (Dobraeus: 'that I do not know').
For guessing is apart from knowing clearly.
That the son of Atreus knows clearly how he is faring.
And it is likely that the father knows.
And I determined that he knows the food.
Knowing the things from outside.
I would speak knowing well the things of the enemy.
Knowing, I would speak.
Knowing well, I have spoken this end.
Knowing this fate, he would pardon mortals.
And knowing my ancient lineage.
So that knowing I may speak more clearly.
The one who knows useful things, not the one who knows many things, is wise.
For to me who knows, this messenger has shouted these tidings.
I speak to one who knows.
Those who know clearly must be angry about these things.
I speak to those who know.
